messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Symptom from test: DOMModelTest.testUnion asserts that the string value of the union /vendor[1]/contact[4] | /vendor[1]/contact[1] is "John". In XPath, converting a node-set to a string returns the string-value of the node that is first in document order. Therefore, the union must be in document order for the correct result.
- Symptom from issue report: string(/MAIN/B | /MAIN/A) returns "b" instead of "avalue", proving that the union result is not in document order but instead reflects operand/insertion order.

- Relevant code path:
  - CoreOperationUnion.computeValue builds an array of EvalContexts for each argument and returns a new UnionContext:
    - It computes each operand expression; if the result is an EvalContext, it uses it directly, otherwise wraps it into a constant context.
    - It then returns new UnionContext(context.getRootContext(), argCtxs).
  - UnionContext constructor (as visible) delegates to its superclass NodeSetContext with a new BasicNodeSet and stores the contexts array:
    - public UnionContext(EvalContext parentContext, EvalContext contexts[]) {
        super(parentContext, new BasicNodeSet());
        this.contexts = contexts;
      }
  - This setup strongly indicates that UnionContext is responsible for iterating over the provided sub-contexts and populating the underlying NodeSet (BasicNodeSet).

- Likely fault:
  - The union implementation in UnionContext merges nodes from its operand contexts into the NodeSet in the order they are traversed (typically left operand first, then right), without reordering by document order.
  - Consequently, when string() is applied to the union, it returns the string-value of the first inserted node (e.g., /MAIN/B from the left operand) rather than the first in document order (which would be /MAIN/A).
  - This exactly matches both the test failure and the issue report’s observed behavior.

- Conclusion:
  - The root cause is that the union operation does not sort the resulting node-set into document order (and possibly does not handle de-duplication consistently).
  - The problem lies in org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.axes.UnionContext: it should ensure that the merged node set is returned in document order. CoreOperationUnion merely delegates to UnionContext; the latter needs to collect nodes from its operand contexts, remove duplicates, and sort by document order (using the framework’s NodePointer comparison facilities) before exposing them to callers or before conversion to string.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

Please provide the full source of org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.axes.UnionContext so I can inspect its iteration and node ordering logic.
CoreOperationUnion.computeValue(org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.EvalContext)
UnionContext.UnionContext(org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.EvalContext, org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.EvalContext[])
